# API Reference

## Main Types

| Type                        | Purpose                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `InfinityValue`             | Large-number value type.                                                                                                    |
| `InfinityValueUnitNames`    | Instance-owned unit suffix table for parsing and display.                                                                   |
| `InfinityValueConverter`    | Optional Newtonsoft.Json converter.                                                                                         |
| `SerializableInfinityValue` | Serialization wrapper for exposing `InfinityValue` in the Unity Inspector ([details](/infinity-value/en/api/inspector.md)). |

## Constructors

```csharp
new InfinityValue(long number)
new InfinityValue(long number, InfinityValueUnitNames unitNames)

new InfinityValue(double number)
new InfinityValue(double number, InfinityValueUnitNames unitNames)

new InfinityValue(float number)
new InfinityValue(float number, InfinityValueUnitNames unitNames)

new InfinityValue(BigInteger number)
new InfinityValue(BigInteger number, InfinityValueUnitNames unitNames)

new InfinityValue(string input)
new InfinityValue(string input, InfinityValueUnitNames unitNames)
```

## Static Values

```csharp
InfinityValue.Zero
InfinityValue.One
```

Use `WithUnitNames` when a zero or one value should carry a custom unit context:

```csharp
InfinityValue zeroGold = InfinityValue.Zero.WithUnitNames(goldUnits);
```

## Parsing

```csharp
InfinityValue.TryParse(string input, out InfinityValue result)
InfinityValue.TryParse(string input, InfinityValueUnitNames unitNames, out InfinityValue result)
```

## Instance Members

```csharp
bool IsEmpty { get; }
InfinityValueUnitNames UnitNames { get; }
InfinityValue WithUnitNames(InfinityValueUnitNames unitNames)
string ToString()
int CompareTo(InfinityValue other)
bool Equals(InfinityValue other)
int GetHashCode()
```

## Operators

```csharp
a + b
a - b
a * 10L
a * 1.5
a / 2L
a / 2.0

a == b
a != b
a < b
a > b
a <= b
a >= b
```

## Conversions

```csharp
InfinityValue value = 1000;
InfinityValue parsed = "500A";

long asLong = (long)value;
double asDouble = (double)value;
float asFloat = (float)value;
```

## See Also

- [Math Helpers](/infinity-value/en/api/math.md) — cost curves, `AffordableCount`, `ToProgress`, `Min`/`Max`/`Clamp`, increment/decrement operators
- [Inspector & Exact Serialization](/infinity-value/en/api/inspector.md) — `SerializableInfinityValue`, `ToExactString`/`TryParseExact`

# Inspector & Exact Serialization

`InfinityValue` is stored internally as 8 `(int, long)` tuples, which Unity's serialization system cannot handle directly. `SerializableInfinityValue` wraps it as a single lossless string and provides a custom `PropertyDrawer` for Inspector editing.

## SerializableInfinityValue

Wrap `InfinityValue` in `SerializableInfinityValue` to expose it as a `MonoBehaviour` or `ScriptableObject` field.

```csharp
using Achieve.InfinityValue;
using UnityEngine;

public class PlayerStats : MonoBehaviour
{
    [SerializeField] private SerializableInfinityValue _gold;

    public InfinityValue Gold => _gold.Value;
}
```

In the Inspector, you can type compact notation like `5.3B`; the `PropertyDrawer` parses it and stores the exact underlying value.

It implicitly converts to and from `InfinityValue`, so you rarely need to write `.Value` explicitly.

```csharp
InfinityValue current = _gold; // implicit conversion
_gold = current + reward;      // InfinityValue -> SerializableInfinityValue
```

Unit names are not part of the serialized data — restored values always use `InfinityValueUnitNames.Default`. Apply `WithUnitNames` after loading if you need per-content unit names.

## ToExactString / TryParseExact

`ToString()` rounds for display, but `ToExactString` serializes a value to a string with no precision loss. It's the same format `SerializableInfinityValue` uses internally, and you can use it directly if you're building your own save system.

```csharp
InfinityValue value = new InfinityValue("5.30B");

string exact = value.ToExactString();
bool ok = InfinityValue.TryParseExact(exact, InfinityValueUnitNames.Default, out var restored);
```

`ToExactString` does not include unit names, so re-apply `WithUnitNames` after restoring a value if you need per-content unit names.

# JSON

When Unity's `com.unity.nuget.newtonsoft-json` package is installed, `InfinityValue` is decorated with `InfinityValueConverter`.

The converter stores values as strings:

```json
{
  "gold": "5.30B"
}
```

## Example

```csharp
using Achieve.InfinityValue;
using Newtonsoft.Json;

public sealed class SaveData
{
    public InfinityValue Gold;
}

var units = new InfinityValueUnitNames(new[] { "", "K", "M", "B" });
var save = new SaveData
{
    Gold = new InfinityValue("5B", units)
};

string json = JsonConvert.SerializeObject(save);
SaveData loaded = JsonConvert.DeserializeObject<SaveData>(json);
```

The default converter reconstructs values with the default unit names. If a save file uses custom unit names, store enough content metadata to choose the correct `InfinityValueUnitNames` when loading gameplay data.

# Math Helpers

Helpers for cost curves, progress bars, and min/max/clamp — the calculations idle and incremental games reach for constantly. All of them work without converting through `double`, and stay overflow-free even for values beyond the 8 unit slots.

## Cost-Curve Math

`Log10`, `Pow`, and `Sqrt` compute in log space, so they stay precise even for very large values.

```csharp
InfinityValue cost = new InfinityValue("1.5B");

double log10 = cost.Log10();       // approximate base-10 logarithm
InfinityValue squared = cost.Pow(2);
InfinityValue sqrt = cost.Sqrt();  // shorthand for Pow(0.5)
```

Useful for upgrade cost curves of the form `baseCost * growthRate^level`:

```csharp
InfinityValue baseCost = new InfinityValue("100");
double growthRate = 1.07;
int level = 42;

InfinityValue costAtLevel = baseCost * Math.Pow(growthRate, level);
```

## Buy-Max Count

`AffordableCount` solves the geometric-series price curve (`baseCost * growthRate^n`) for how many items a given balance can afford. Use it to implement a "buy max" button.

```csharp
InfinityValue balance = new InfinityValue("50K");
InfinityValue baseCost = new InfinityValue("100");
double growthRate = 1.07;

long affordable = InfinityValue.AffordableCount(balance, baseCost, growthRate);
```

- `growthRate` must be greater than 1.
- `baseCost` must be greater than 0.
- Returns `0` if `balance` is less than `baseCost`.

## Progress

`ToProgress` returns the current value's progress toward `max` as an overflow-free `float` between 0 and 1. It's a pure function safe to call every frame, for health bars, experience bars, and similar UI.

```csharp
InfinityValue exp = new InfinityValue("750");
InfinityValue expToNextLevel = new InfinityValue("1000");

float progress = exp.ToProgress(expToNextLevel); // 0.75f
```

## Min / Max / Clamp

```csharp
InfinityValue lower = InfinityValue.Min(a, b);
InfinityValue upper = InfinityValue.Max(a, b);
InfinityValue clamped = InfinityValue.Clamp(value, min, max);
```

## Increment / Decrement Operators

```csharp
InfinityValue count = new InfinityValue("10");
count++; // count + 1
count--; // count - 1
```

As with subtraction, a decrement that would go negative clamps to zero.

# Unit Names

`InfinityValueUnitNames` is an instance object. It replaces the old global configuration style and lets each content system own its own suffix table.

## Default Units

The default table starts with an empty base unit and continues with `A`, `B`, `C` through `CZ`.

```csharp
InfinityValue value = new InfinityValue(1_500_000L);
Debug.Log(value); // 1.50B
```

## Custom Units

Index 0 must be an empty string because it represents the base number tier.

```csharp
var units = new InfinityValueUnitNames(new[]
{
    "", "K", "M", "B", "T", "Qa", "Qi", "Sx"
});

InfinityValue value = new InfinityValue(5_300_000_000L, units);
Debug.Log(value); // 5.30B
```

## Multiple Content Tables

Different content can keep different names without touching global state.

```csharp
var currencyUnits = new InfinityValueUnitNames(new[] { "", "K", "M", "B" });
var damageUnits = new InfinityValueUnitNames(new[] { "", "a", "b", "c" });

InfinityValue gold = new InfinityValue("12K", currencyUnits);
InfinityValue damage = new InfinityValue("12a", damageUnits);
```

## Parsing

Always parse saved strings with the same unit table that created them.

```csharp
if (InfinityValue.TryParse("42M", currencyUnits, out var value))
    Debug.Log(value);
```

## Validation

`InfinityValueUnitNames` throws an exception when:

- The name list is null.
- The list is empty.
- Index 0 is not an empty string.
- A unit name is null.
- A unit name appears more than once.

# Changelog

## Unreleased

## 1.2.2 — 2026-07-11

- Added `Pow`, `Sqrt`, and `Log10` for cost-curve math without overflowing `double`.
- Added `AffordableCount` to solve the geometric-series "buy max" formula for a price curve `baseCost * growthRate^n`.
- Added `Min`, `Max`, and `Clamp` static helpers.
- Added `operator ++` and `operator --`.
- Added `ToProgress` for safe, overflow-free 0-1 progress bar values.
- Added `SerializableInfinityValue` for exposing `InfinityValue` fields in the Unity Inspector, with a custom `PropertyDrawer` that accepts compact notation (e.g. `5.3B`) and a lossless `ToExactString`/`TryParseExact` round-trip.
- Added `Editor/Achieve.InfinityValue.Editor.asmdef` for editor-only inspector code.

## 1.2.1 — 2026-07-07

- Normalized the `author` field in `package.json` to the object schema (`{ "name": "Achieveone" }`) expected by Unity Package Manager / OpenUPM.

## 1.2.0 — 2026-06-14

- Added `InfinityValueUnitNames` for per-content unit name instances.
- Added constructor and `TryParse` overloads that accept `InfinityValueUnitNames`.
- Fixed parsing for compact decimal strings such as `5.30B`.
- Rebuilt documentation as GitBook-friendly Markdown plus VitePress deployment.
- Added Unity Package Manager samples under `Samples~`.

## 1.1.0 — 2026-05-23

- Fixed semantic equality and hashing for values with different internal slot order.
- Fixed subtraction borrow behavior and negative-result clamping.
- Added `TryParse`, `Zero`, `One`, double operations, and double conversion.

## 1.0.1 — 2026-01-04

- Reduced GC pressure through internal structural optimizations.

## 1.0.0 — 2024-09-17

- Initial release.

# Getting Started

## Install

Add the package through Unity Package Manager:

```text
https://github.com/achieveonepark/infinity-value.git
```

Or add it to `Packages/manifest.json`:

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "com.achieve.infinity-value": "https://github.com/achieveonepark/infinity-value.git"
  }
}
```

## Create Values

```csharp
using Achieve.InfinityValue;

InfinityValue a = 1000;
InfinityValue b = new InfinityValue(1_500_000L);
InfinityValue c = new InfinityValue(1.5e12);
InfinityValue d = new InfinityValue("300B 200A");
```

## Use Per-Content Unit Names

Use `InfinityValueUnitNames` when different systems need different suffixes.

```csharp
var currencyUnits = new InfinityValueUnitNames(new[]
{
    "", "K", "M", "B", "T", "Qa", "Qi"
});

var damageUnits = new InfinityValueUnitNames(new[]
{
    "", "a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f"
});

InfinityValue gold = new InfinityValue("12K", currencyUnits);
InfinityValue damage = new InfinityValue("12a", damageUnits);
```

Each `InfinityValue` carries the unit name instance that was passed to it. Arithmetic keeps the left-hand value's unit names:

```csharp
InfinityValue totalGold = gold + new InfinityValue(5000, currencyUnits);
Debug.Log(totalGold); // 17.00K
```

## Parse Safely

```csharp
if (!InfinityValue.TryParse("5B", currencyUnits, out var parsed))
    parsed = InfinityValue.Zero.WithUnitNames(currencyUnits);
```

## Save And Load

The simplest persistence format is the display string plus the same unit name set on load:

```csharp
PlayerPrefs.SetString("gold", gold.ToString());

string raw = PlayerPrefs.GetString("gold", "0");
InfinityValue.TryParse(raw, currencyUnits, out gold);
```

# Introduction

Infinity Value is a Unity package for idle and incremental games that need numbers far beyond `long`.

Values are stored as compact `(unitIndex, value)` pairs, so common arithmetic and comparison work without allocating managed garbage. Display and parsing can use the built-in `A, B, C ... CZ` unit names, or a custom `InfinityValueUnitNames` instance per content type.

```csharp
using Achieve.InfinityValue;

var goldUnits = new InfinityValueUnitNames(new[]
{
    "", "K", "M", "B", "T", "Qa", "Qi"
});

InfinityValue gold = new InfinityValue(5_300_000_000L, goldUnits);
InfinityValue reward = new InfinityValue("12K", goldUnits);

gold += reward;

Debug.Log(gold.ToString()); // 5.30B
```

## Highlights

- Struct-based large number type for Unity runtime code.
- Arithmetic: `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`.
- Comparison: `==`, `!=`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`.
- Instance unit names through `InfinityValueUnitNames`.
- String parsing with `TryParse`.
- Optional Newtonsoft.Json converter when Unity's Newtonsoft package is installed.
- Importable Unity samples under `Samples~`.

# Usage

The package includes importable samples through Unity Package Manager.

## Basic Usage

Shows construction, arithmetic, comparison, and display.

Import path:

```text
Samples~/Basic Usage
```

## Content Unit Names

Shows ScriptableObject-style content instances that own their own `InfinityValueUnitNames`.

Import path:

```text
Samples~/Content Unit Names
```

## Save Load

Shows simple PlayerPrefs persistence using `TryParse`.

Import path:

```text
Samples~/Save Load
```
